FACTUAL POSITION
& PLEADINGS

1. Vide this judgment/award, this Tribunal shall decide claim of compensation on account of death of Master Manish in a road vehicular accident which took place on 18.05.2019 at about 4:30 AM at Ganj Muradabad, Agra Lucknow Expressway within jurisdiction of PS Bhangarmau, Unnao UP.
CASE OF PETITIONER SIDE 2.

Succinctly, the case put forward vide petition is that on 18.05.2019, deceased along with his parents and many other people were travelling from Gurugram to Madhubani, Bihar in a Bus bearing registration No. UP83BT4106 driven by respondent Sh Vishnudev Sah And Anr vs Bijoy Mondal Andn Ors on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195879136/
3 no.1.

Respondent no.1 was driving it at very high speed and was not following traffic rules &
regulations.

The respondent no.1 while driving the bus in aforesaid manner, hit one tractor trolley loaded with watermelons from behind at about 4:30 AM when it was travelling in area of Ganj Muradabad on Agra Lucknow Expressway at Bhangarmau, District Unnao, UP.
The respondent no.1 was not able to control it after same and it turned turtle at the spot of incident resulting in severe injuries to the passengers travelling in it including the deceased.
After the incident, all injured were shifted to Government Hospital, Unnao.
Deceased expired during the treatment.
The incident happened solely due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.01.
Deceased was aged about 12 years and was studying at the time of incident.
The respondent no.01 being driver, the respondent no.02 being owner and respondent no.03 being the insurer of offending Vishnudev Sah & Anr.

The petitioner(s) is/are certainly entitled for compensation in view of decision of above issue.

(iv). The amount of notional income thus calculated shall be reduced to two-third, the deduction to the extent of one- third being towards personal & living expenses of the deceased, the balance taken as the annual loss to estate (hereinafter also referred to as "the multiplicand").

(v). For assessment of the pecuniary damages on account of the death of children upto the age of 10 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated, capitalizing the multiplicand, by applying the multiplier of ten (10).
(vi). For children of the age-group of more than 10 years upto 15 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated by applying the multiplier of fifteen (15).
(vii). For children of the age-group of more than 15 years but less than 18 years, the loss to estate shall be calculated by applying the multiplier of eighteen (18).

sentences.text: The petitioner(s), in the claim petition has/have claimed that the deceased was aged about 12 years on the date of accident.
The date of incident is 18.05.2019.
As per Post Mortem report of deceased, the deceased was aged about 12 years at the time of incident.
Hence, deceased was 12 years of age at the time of incident and his age is considered accordingly.
He falls in age bracket upto 15 years, hence, multiplier applicable in this matter as per above judgment would be 15.
COMPUTATION OF AWARD 11.4

In view of the abovesaid judgment, the notional income of the minor has to be computed as Rs.15,000/- X A (Cost Inflation Index for the financial year in which the accident occurred) /331 (CII for the base year 1997-1998).
11.5 CBDT has notified the CII vide circular bearing No. SO1790(E) on 05.06.2017.
The major change in this notification is the introduction of new base year as financial year 2001-2002 instead of financial year 1981-1982.
CII has been notified as 289 for the financial year 2019-20 and the CII for the base year 2001- 2002 is 100.

Accordingly, the formula which has been stated in the said authority needs to be read as under:-
"Rs.15,000/- x 289 (CII for the year 2019- 2020) /100".
11.6
Thus, Notional Annual Income of the deceased comes out to be Rs.43,350/- [Rs.15000/-X 289(CII for the year 2019-2020)/100] 11.7

By virtue of para no. 71 (iv) of the said judgment, the said notional income is to be reduced to 2/3rd after deducting 1/3 towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and the Vishnudev Sah & Anr. vs. Bijoy Mondal & Ors.

11.9 Considering above, the total loss of the estate would come to Rs. Rs.4,33,500/-=(Rs.28,900/- x 15).
11.10 Furthermore, by virtue of para no. 71(viii), of the said judgment, a sum equal to loss of estate i.e. Rs. 4,33,500/- needs to be added towards non pecuniary damages.

11.11 So, the total loss of estate and pecuniary damages would come out to be Rs.4,33,500/- + Rs.4,33,500/- =
Rs.8,67,000/-.
TOTAL AWARD AMOUNT OF ALL HEADS 11.12

After completion of pleadings, on 05.04.2022, the scholarly predecessor of this tribunal framed following issues:-
1. Whether the deceased Master Manish suffered fatal injuries in the accident that took place on 18.05.2019 at about 4:30 AM due to rash and negligent driving of Bus bearing registration number UP83BT4106 by the respondent no.1. Bijoy Mondal,
being owned by the respondent no.2 N. K. Traders and insured with the respondent no.3?

ANALYSIS/FINDINGS ON ISSUES Issue No.(1) - Whether the deceased Master Manish suffered fatal injuries in the accident that took place on 18.05.2019 at about 4:30 AM due to rash and negligent driving of Bus bearing registration number UP83BT4106 by the respondent no.1.
10.1 Before adverting to the facts of the present petition for deciding the above issue, at the very outset, it would be apposite to note here that the procedure followed by an accident Vishnudev Sah & Anr. vs. Bijoy Mondal & Ors.
10.5 In totality of circumstances, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the claimant side has been able to bring on record such facts which proves almost at the scales of preponderance of probabilities that the incident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle Sh Vishnudev Sah And Anr vs Bijoy Mondal Andn Ors on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/195879136/
Issue No.(2) - Whether the petitioners/claimants are entitled to compensation, if yes, of what amount and from whom?
Before proceeding further to decide the present issue, it would be apposite to encapsulate the law laid down by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in its guiding lamp post judgment qua methodology and considerations for assessing/ascertaining just compensation in road vehicular death cases of minors as it is pleaded that deceased was 08 years of age at the time of incident.
"71. Subject to all other requisite conditions being fulfilled, for the foregoing reasons,
in order to bring about consistency and uniformity in approach to the issue, it is held that claims for compensation on account of death of children shall be determined as follows :
(i). Till such time as the law is amended by the legislature, or the Central Government notifies the amendment to the Second chedule in exercise of the enabling power vested in it by Section 163-A (3) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, and except in cases wherein the prospects of employability and earnings (in future or present) of the deceased child are proved by cogent and irrefutable evidence, this having regard,
inter alia, to the academic record or training in special talents or skills, for computing the pecuniary damages on account of the loss to estate, the notional income of non- earning persons (`15000/- p.a.) as specified in the Second Schedule (brought in force from 14.11.1994), shall be assumed to be the income of the deceased child, and taken into account after it is inflation- corrected with the help of Cost Inflation Index (CII) as notified by the Government of India from year to year under Section 48 of the Income Tax Act, 1961, by applying the formula indicated hereinafter.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In civil matters the facts are required to be established by way of preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubt as is required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is not as heavy as it is in a criminal case and in a claim petition under The Motor Vehicles Act, 1988,
this burden is even lesser than a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the prepositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case of "Bimla Devi and others Vs.
Himachal Road Transport Corporation and Ors." reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgments in the case of "Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and Ors." 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and "Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. &
Ors.", 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303 etc. 10.2

It is also evident from the fact that not only he hit the bus in tractor trolley from behind but he was also not able to control it after the incident, due to which, it turned turtle.
The circumstances of the incident leaves no doubt that incident happened due to negligence of respondent no.1 only.

The vehicle in question certainly had valid national permit.
The authorization required to ply the vehicle in a particular State applies only when such vehicle is plied outside the jurisdiction of the State where it is registered.
